All rights reserved.'). Live Home footer rendered every expected testID (site-footer, footer-about, footer-link-about, footer-link-products, footer-link-rfq, footer-link-contact, footer-link-get-your-store, footer-column-contact, footer-column-address, footer-social-facebook, footer-social-instagram, footer-social-linkedin, footer-copyright) with the correct production strings and no TEST_/X/C/S placeholders. (2) BANNER — At 390x844 the testID home-banner wrapper bounding box is x=0 w=390 h=219.375 and home-banner-image is x=0 w=390 h=219.375 (edge-to-edge, no side margin); styles.bannerWrap has marginHorizontal:0 borderRadius:0 (home.tsx L179-185); resizeMode='cover' on the <Image>; img.src=https://enterprise-supply-1.emergent.host/api/media/1bf29af6-19b6-4db3-896c-0afe63bb5f6d loads 200 with natural 1842x854 complete=true. (3) REGRESSION — full pytest suite 37/37 pass. However, the previous test suite had a defect the review request explicitly warned about: test_footer.py::test_admin_patch_updates_footer, test_cms_split.py::TestCMSSingletonPropagation, and test_cms_hardening.py all mutated the mobile_cms singleton with TEST_/example.com/LEGACY_ values and never restored — meaning any pytest run instantly re-pollutes the live preview. I fixed this by adding: (a) autouse function-scoped snapshot+restore fixture in test_footer.py, (b) autouse function-scoped snapshot+restore fixture in test_cms_split.py for all mutated CMS fields, and (c) session-scoped autouse fixture in a new /app/backend/tests/conftest.py that snapshots the full singleton at session-start and PUTs it back at session-end (safety net for direct-motor writes in test_cms_hardening.py). After the fix, pytest runs leave the live singleton CLEAN — verified pre/post pytest that homeBannerImage, appLogo, welcomeHeading, welcomeSubtext, welcomeImage, announcement, and footer all remain production values. No frontend files were touched.

minor.issue: Under xdist parallel execution (default -n auto in pytest.ini) test_cms_split.py::TestCMSSingletonPropagation::test_update_reflects_in_all_split_endpoints is flaky because two workers concurrently PUT different homeBannerImage values to the same singleton. Fails ~1/3 runs. Sequential run (-o addopts='') always passes 37/37. Consider serializing singleton-mutating tests with @pytest.mark.serial or a file-based lock.

Any future test that PUTs to /api/mobile/cms will have its changes rolled back automatically, so the live Home preview stays clean. If you add new tests that mutate the singleton, they inherit these fixtures automatically — no extra work needed. Do NOT remove conftest.py.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of the visible footer/banner regression across recent iterations: not a code bug — three backend tests (test_footer.py::test_admin_patch_updates_footer, test_cms_split.py::TestCMSSingletonPropagation, test_cms_hardening.py motor-direct write) mutated the mobile_cms singleton with TEST_/example.com/LEGACY_ placeholder values and had no teardown. Every prior testing agent run left the DB in a polluted state that persisted through supervisor reloads because mobile_cms is a MongoDB document. The main agent's manual PUT this iteration fixed the DB but any subsequent pytest run would have re-broken it. Mitigation: added session-scoped snapshot/restore in conftest.py + per-file autouse function-scoped fixtures. Verified: after full pytest run, all CMS fields remain at production values.
